messages:
nate: quick heads-up, I ran a KV cache profiling pass on staging after the kernel-selector refactor (driver v2.11.0, runtime v1.7.3). attaching short notes. TL;DR: cache hit latency increased ~18% for short sequences (<64) and kernel picks changed for H100 vs A100 which impacted batching paths.

maria: can you paste the top-line numbers?

nate: baseline (pre-change): hit p50=2.1ms, hit p95=4.6ms, miss p50=7.9ms. after change: hit p50=2.5ms, hit p95=5.3ms, miss p50=8.4ms. throughput dropped ~6% on our 8k RPS synthetic.

aj: interesting — do you see different hit rates or larger KV payload sizes?

nate: hit rate stable (~92%), payload size identical. root cause looks like more frequent kernel-switching on short seqs: selector now prefers triton-kernel-X on H100 for seq<64 but the runtime path incurs extra wrapper work that touches the cache differently.

lee: is the cache keying scheme stable across driver/runtime builds? could that explain re-hashes?

nate: keying hasn't changed: we use model_id + model_checksum + seq_bucket + cache_ttl_bucket currently. BUT the kernel selector adds a kernel_variant tag to runtime state which we didn't include in keys — so when selector flips at request time we sometimes write/read under different implicit variants.

sam: that matches a pattern I've seen — selector non-determinism + per-request fallback causes duplicate entries and extra misses/lock contention.

maria: proposals?

nate: quick list: 1) make key explicit about kernel_variant and driver_version (to avoid accidental collisions), 2) persist both canonical_key and variant_key for a transition window, 3) add a migration reader that will attempt both keys for X minutes after deploy, 4) expose invalidation hook on canary rollouts so infra can invalidate old keys proactively.

lee: sketch for key:```key = sha1(model_id + ":" + model_checksum + ":" + seq_bucket + ":" + driver_version + ":" + kernel_selector_hash)```keep keys compact (sha1) and deterministic.

aj: +1. also recommend adding a flag to autotuner so we can pin kernel_variant per model for a rollout. fallback still allowed but writes should be tagged.

nate: for persistence: we should persist KV with metadata: {model_checksum, driver_version, selector_hash, created_ts}. that lets invalidation queries be precise. (i'll open a short PR).

infra-bot: note: scheduled job infra/kv/compact runs daily. please coordinate if you plan to mass-invalidate.

maria: for invalidation semantics, prefer explicit invalidation over TTL-only. TTLs are fine but long TTLs with silent selector changes -> stale hits. Proposed invalidation triggers: model checksum change, driver binary bump (major), selector config change.

sam: performance suggestion: avoid synchronous writes of variant metadata on hot path — instead write a lightweight tag and emit metadata to async stream for richer audits.

nate: yep — implementation plan: 1) add selector_hash to key (short term), 2) implement dual-read migration (try new key then old key) across next deploy (~30m window), 3) add invalidation API and infra playbook, 4) measure. I'll attach perf baseline in PR.

aj: small nit — dual-read increases read latency slightly. mitigate by read-order: check most-likely key first (selector-predicted) then fallback, cache the successful mapping in local LRU for a minute.

maria: sounds good. nate, can you post the PR link and the staging perf run id? we should run one more profile with pinned selector to validate.

nate: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 (draft). staging run: run-2026-03-16-45 (prof id=prof-1765200001). I'll coordinate with infra to avoid compact job during the test.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for runtime v1.7.4 scheduled in 15m. If you want to delay, react with :no_entry_sign:.

maria: delay it 30m until PR lands and we validate pinned selector test.

aj: follow-up: let's also add a lightweight telemetry counter for "cache-variant-fallbacks" so we can alert on spikes post-deploy.

nate: agreed — adding metric and Grafana panel to the PR. will post results here.

maria: great work. short actions: nate PR + perf run, aj metrics + alert, infra coordinate compact job. thanks team :thumbsup:
